sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: People who make horror movies know that if you want to scare someone, use scary music.
sentences.zh: 制作恐怖电影的人都知道，如果你想吓唬别人，就用恐怖的音乐。

sentences.en: And when we want to explore the design of music, we call Rishikesh Herway from the podcast Song Exploder.
sentences.zh: 而当我们想要探索音乐的设计时，我们会邀请播客《歌曲解密》的里希克什·赫尔威。

sentences.en: So here are two fundamental ways to make something sound scary, according to evolutionary biologist Dan Blumstein.
sentences.zh: 根据演化生物学家丹·布卢姆斯坦的说法，让声音听起来可怕主要有两种基本方法。

sentences.en: The first way is to use lots of screechy, irregular tones.
sentences.zh: 第一种方法是使用大量刺耳、不规则的音调。

sentences.en: Well, the animals, when they're scared, are blowing a lot of air across their vocal cords, or across their syrinx if they're a bird.
sentences.zh: 动物在害怕时，会把大量气流穿过声带，如果它们是鸟类，则是穿过鸣管。

sentences.en: And the sounds of screams are something that is arousing and makes people feel negative.
sentences.zh: 尖叫声能唤起情绪，并让人产生消极的感受。

sentences.en: It's biological.
sentences.zh: 这是生物学现象。

sentences.en: Your lizard brain hears Bernard Herrmann's knife-stabbing music in Psycho and says,
sentences.zh: 你体内的爬行动物脑一听到《惊魂记》中伯纳德·赫尔曼的刺刀音乐，就会发出信号：

sentences.en: Something terrible is happening right now.
sentences.zh: 现在正发生可怕的事情。

sentences.en: The second way sounds can make you feel uneasy is to go the other way.
sentences.zh: 声音让人感到不安的第二种方法则是走向另一个极端。

sentences.en: Make really low, grumbling sounds with lots of bass.
sentences.zh: 制造带有大量低音的、非常低沉的隆隆声。

sentences.en: Another biological cue that might lead to fear and anxiety is hearing low frequencies.
sentences.zh: 另一个可能导致恐惧和焦虑的生物学线索是听到低频声音。

sentences.en: The lowest frequency a species can produce is a function of its body size.
sentences.zh: 一个物种能够产生的最低频率与其体型大小有关。

sentences.en: So low frequency probably should scare you.
sentences.zh: 所以低频声音大概率会吓到你。

sentences.en: It might mean that something big is around.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着有什么庞然大物在附近。

sentences.en: Mix those both together and you're on your way to creating classic scary music for scary movies.
sentences.zh: 把这两者结合起来，你就走上了为恐怖电影创作经典恐怖音乐的道路。

sentences.en: But horror movies aren't just meant to be horrifying.
sentences.zh: 但恐怖电影不仅仅是为了吓人。

sentences.en: They're also meant to be exciting and fun.
sentences.zh: 它们也旨在令人兴奋和有趣。

sentences.en: So it's sometimes nice to have a driving beat.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候配上有推动力的节拍会很不错。

sentences.en: The music from the movie Halloween by composer John Carpenter will always creep me out.
sentences.zh: 由作曲家约翰·卡朋特为电影《月光光心慌慌》创作的音乐总是让我毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: And also get me kind of excited.
sentences.zh: 同时也让我感到有点兴奋。

sentences.en: In terms of horror movies, I certainly know that I respond to sound in horror movies in ways that are complex.
sentences.zh: 就恐怖电影而言，我确实知道我对恐怖电影中声音的反应是复杂的。

sentences.en: You know, John Carpenter's soundtracks are, you know, a good example.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，约翰·卡朋特的配乐就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: You know, that's a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那是一种非常具体的东西。

sentences.en: It evokes dread.
sentences.zh: 它唤起了恐惧感。

sentences.en: David Slade is very good at evoking dread himself.
sentences.zh: 大卫·斯莱德本人就非常擅长唤起恐惧感。

sentences.en: My name's David Slade.
sentences.zh: 我叫大卫·斯莱德。

sentences.en: I directed the pilot for the first episode of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 我执导了《汉尼拔》第一集的试播集。

sentences.en: And I'm an executive producer on the show.
sentences.zh: 我是这部剧的执行制片人。

sentences.en: And I pretty much sound mix every episode.
sentences.zh: 而且我几乎为每一集都做过声音混音。

sentences.en: I've been binging on the TV show Hannibal for the past couple weeks.
sentences.zh: 过去几周我一直在刷电视剧《汉尼拔》。

sentences.en: And it really gets under your skin.
sentences.zh: 它真的深入人心。

sentences.en: It's the story of a serial killer named Hannibal Lecter, who you may know from Silence of the Lambs and Manhunter.
sentences.zh: 故事讲述了一个名叫汉尼拔·莱克特的连环杀手，你可能从《沉默的羔羊》和《猎人》中知道他。

sentences.en: This is kind of a prequel to those stories.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是这些故事的前传。

sentences.en: Hannibal is a nasty character who commits grisly and unspeakable crimes.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔是一个犯下可怕且不可言说的罪行的讨厌角色。

sentences.en: The other main character is Will Graham, an FBI profiler who has a knack for getting inside the heads of serial killers to try to catch them.
sentences.zh: 另一个主角是威尔·格雷厄姆，一名FBI心理侧写师，他有一种进入连环杀手内心以试图抓获他们的特长。

sentences.en: Trust me, there is nothing fun going on inside Will Graham's head.
sentences.zh: 相信我，威尔·格雷厄姆的内心世界里绝对没有好玩的事。

sentences.en: And inside Will Graham's head is exactly where the sound design of Hannibal is trying to place the viewer.
sentences.zh: 而威尔·格雷厄姆的内心深处，正是《汉尼拔》的声音设计试图将观众置身的地方。

sentences.en: Will Graham visualizes things and he recognizes patterns.
sentences.zh: 威尔·格雷厄姆能将事物视觉化，并且他能识别模式。

sentences.en: This is what he does.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所做的事情。

sentences.en: He reconstructs things in his head.
sentences.zh: 他在脑海中重构事物。

sentences.en: It's a mental activity.
sentences.zh: 这是一种精神活动。

sentences.en: Synapsis firing.
sentences.zh: 突触在放电。

sentences.en: These are things that we want to make an audio analog of.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们想要制作出音频模拟的东西。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of like...
sentences.zh: 所以有很多类似于……

sentences.en: ...sounds.
sentences.zh: ……的声音。

sentences.en: This is from the first episode of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 这段来自《汉尼拔》的第一集。

sentences.en: All the classic horror movie music we mentioned before exists outside the world of the story.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过的所有经典恐怖电影音乐都存在于故事世界之外。

sentences.en: In other words, it's not being heard by the characters being depicted.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，正在被描绘的角色们并没有听到这些音乐。

sentences.en: It's just being heard by the audience.
sentences.zh: 只有观众能听到。

sentences.en: But composer Brian Reitzel's score for Hannibal feels different.
sentences.zh: 但作曲家布莱恩·雷策尔为《汉尼拔》创作的配乐感觉却有所不同。

sentences.en: You get a sense that it's even being heard by Will Graham inside his own imagination.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得甚至连威尔·格雷厄姆在他自己的想象中也能听到这些声音。

sentences.en: Our whole goal with horror really is to transport people into this other reality.
sentences.zh: 我们处理恐怖题材的整体目标实际上是将人们带入另一个现实。

sentences.en: And it's a scary reality.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的现实。

sentences.en: It's a tense reality.
sentences.zh: 这是一个紧张的现实。

sentences.en: But it's a beautiful place, too.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一个美丽的地方。

sentences.en: But to do that, I find the most effective way to scare people is to throw sounds at them that are unfamiliar to them.
sentences.zh: 但要做到这一点，我发现吓唬人最有效的方法是向他们抛出他们不熟悉的声音。

sentences.en: So Brian constructs new sounds that the audience can't place to create unease.
sentences.zh: 因此，布莱恩构建了观众无法定位的新声音，从而营造出不安感。

sentences.en: That's not a guitar.
sentences.zh: 那不是吉他。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: A lot of what we do is create all of the sound.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的大部分工作是创作所有的声音。

sentences.en: So we turn all the sound effects off.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把所有的音效都关掉。

sentences.en: And the ones that we think are important, we try to make something that resembles that sound or feels like that sound.
sentences.zh: 对于我们认为重要的那些，我们试图创造出类似于那种声音或感觉像那种声音的东西。

sentences.en: I don't differentiate really between ambient sounds, like a motor and a bass.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不区分环境音，比如马达声和低音。

sentences.en: So in this case, he's on a motorcycle.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，他正骑着摩托车。

sentences.en: I thought it would be really interesting to make the feeling of what it would be like being on that motorcycle.
sentences.zh: 我觉得创造身处那辆摩托车上的感觉会非常有趣。

sentences.en: Rush of adrenaline and the wind and the sound of the engine, which is underneath you.
sentences.zh: 肾上腺素的涌动、风声以及位于你身下的发动机轰鸣声。

sentences.en: I mean, all this is very powerful stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些都是非常有力量的东西。

sentences.en: So the first idea I had was to do it with an upright bass, just glistening up and down the neck, kind of revving.
sentences.zh: 所以我脑海中的第一个想法是用低音提琴来表现，琴弓在琴颈上下摩擦，有点像在轰鸣引擎。

sentences.en: The cue starts with the motorcycle starting up.
sentences.zh: 音乐伴随着摩托车的启动而开始。

sentences.en: So we do lots of little things in there to mimic or hint at those sounds.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在里面做了很多小动作来模仿或暗示这些声音。

sentences.en: On screen, we're seeing the key turn castanets.
sentences.zh: 在屏幕上，我们看到钥匙转动响板。

sentences.en: Then we see the flames from the engine.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到了来自发动机的火焰。

sentences.en: The sound of heat is me bowing a woodblock.
sentences.zh: 热度的声音是我用弓拉木鱼发出的。

sentences.en: It puts some reverb on it and it sounds like smoke.
sentences.zh: 它给声音加了一些混响，听起来就像烟雾一样。

sentences.en: The more I work with the different instruments, the more I understand what you can get out of them.
sentences.zh: 我越是和不同的乐器合作，就越能理解你能从中获得什么。

sentences.en: Almost all the sounds in Hannibal's start out as an acoustic element from Brian Reitzel's workshop.
sentences.zh: 《汉尼拔》中的几乎所有声音都是从布莱恩·雷策尔工作室的声学元素开始的。

sentences.en: Then the effort is made to strip it of identifying characteristics that would ground the sound in the real world.
sentences.zh: 然后努力剥离其身份特征，正是这些特征将声音根植于现实世界中。

sentences.en: I'm constantly trying to de-guitar a guitar or de-drum a drum.
sentences.zh: 我一直在试图消除吉他的吉他味或消除鼓的鼓味。

sentences.en: That's Brian placing a wooden chopstick on a snare drum and pulling a violin bow across the chopstick.
sentences.zh: 那是布莱恩把一根木筷子放在小军鼓上，然后用小提琴弓拉过木筷子。

sentences.en: You could never tell by listening that a chopstick, bow, or a drum made this sound.
sentences.zh: 你听的时候绝对猜不到筷子、琴弓或鼓能发出这种声音。

sentences.en: Brian doesn't just take regular instruments and make them weird.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩不仅是把普通乐器变得古怪。

sentences.en: He also takes weird instruments and makes them weirder.
sentences.zh: 他还把古怪的乐器变得更古怪。

sentences.en: I went around Brian's studio as he pulled out examples of the instruments he uses.
sentences.zh: 我参观了布莱恩的工作室，他拿出了他所使用的乐器范例。

sentences.en: For example, the sound of synapses firing inside Wilgram's head started out as a Newton's cradle.
sentences.zh: 例如，威尔·格雷厄姆脑海中突触放电的声音最初是由牛顿摆开始的。

sentences.en: If you don't know a Newton's cradle by name, you definitely know the sound.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道牛顿摆的名字，你一定知道它的声音。

sentences.en: Right, everybody knows this.
sentences.zh: 没错，大家都知道这个。

sentences.en: It sits on your desk.
sentences.zh: 它就放在你的桌子上。

sentences.en: You know, it's that pendulum toy with the stainless steel balls all hanging from strings.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是那个挂着不锈钢小球的摆锤玩具。

sentences.en: But what I did is I used it to create these rhythms, kind of synapse in your brain stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我所做的是用它来创造这些节奏，有点像你大脑中的突触那样的东西。

sentences.en: And did some different treatments of those and used those as a percussion instrument.
sentences.zh: 并对这些声音进行了不同的处理，将其用作打击乐器。

sentences.en: You can see I actually broke it in the process.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到我在这个过程中其实把它弄坏了。

sentences.en: There were originally five balls that were a perfect unison.
sentences.zh: 原本有五个完全谐振的小球。

sentences.en: Even the most innocuous instruments turned sinister in the hands of Brian Reitzel.
sentences.zh: 在布莱恩·雷策尔手中，即便是最无害的乐器也会变得阴险。

sentences.en: And these sleigh bells I just used in this first episode of Hannibal because I had snails.
sentences.zh: 我之所以在《汉尼拔》的第一集里用到这些雪橇铃，是因为我有蜗牛的镜头。

sentences.en: And I had these macro shots of snails.
sentences.zh: 我有这些蜗牛的微距镜头。

sentences.en: But really, it's these sleigh bells.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这就是这些雪橇铃。

sentences.en: And, you know, I can go on and on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我可以滔滔不绝地讲下去。

sentences.en: David Slade calls the sound design of Hannibal free associative.
sentences.zh: 大卫·斯莱德将《汉尼拔》的声音设计称为自由联想。

sentences.en: They look at the footage and talk about the characters and the feelings they're trying to evoke from each scene.
sentences.zh: 他们观看素材，讨论角色以及他们试图从每个场景中唤起的情感。

sentences.en: And design from there.
sentences.zh: 然后从那里开始进行设计。

sentences.en: The big bad guy in Hannibal is, of course, Hannibal Lecter.
sentences.zh: 《汉尼拔》中的大反派当然是汉尼拔·莱克特。

sentences.en: But Wilgram also is wrestling with his own demons.
sentences.zh: 但威尔·格雷厄姆也在与他自己的心魔作斗争。

sentences.en: He has dreamlike visions of a demon they call the Wendigo.
sentences.zh: 他对一个被称为温迪戈的恶魔有着梦幻般的幻觉。

sentences.en: That represents both the evil of Hannibal and the evil growing inside Wilgram.
sentences.zh: 这既代表了汉尼拔的邪恶，也代表了在威尔·格雷厄姆心中滋长的邪恶。

sentences.en: One of the characters that developed over time was the Wendigo character, which is the bassist of horrors.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移发展起来的角色之一就是温迪戈，也就是恐怖的低音贝斯手。

sentences.en: And we wanted a sound that indicated the coming of that character.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一个能够预示该角色来临的声音。

sentences.en: That sound, I knew it was circular.
sentences.zh: 那个声音，我知道它是圆形的。

sentences.en: We didn't know why, but we knew that was right.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道为什么，但我们知道那是对的。

sentences.en: And I took what David said literally and I got a bull roar.
sentences.zh: 我字面理解了大卫说的话，然后我弄来了一个牛吼器。

sentences.en: But basically it's a piece of wood on a string.
sentences.zh: 但基本上它就是一根系在绳子上的木头。

sentences.en: It's one of the oldest instruments.
sentences.zh: 它是最古老的乐器之一。

sentences.en: But it sounds incredible.
sentences.zh: 但它的声音令人难以置信。

sentences.en: You spin it in a circular manner.
sentences.zh: 你以环形的方式旋转它。

sentences.en: And in doing so, it slices through the air, creating this sort of sound.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，它切开空气，创造出这种声音。

sentences.en: Once we put it against the picture, we knew it was the right sound.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们把它放进画面里，我们就知道这是对的声音。

sentences.en: It's very physical sounding, sort of cutting through the air, spinning around your head, making it surreal, yet also very physical.
sentences.zh: 它听起来非常具象，有点像切开空气，在你的头脑周围旋转，既超现实又非常具象。

sentences.en: I also did things to that sound.
sentences.zh: 我对那个声音也做了一些处理。

sentences.en: I pitched it down.
sentences.zh: 我把它的音调降低了。

sentences.en: I pitched it up to make it scarier.
sentences.zh: 我把它的音调升高来让它更吓人。

sentences.en: Well, mission accomplished, guys.
sentences.zh: 好吧，任务完成了，伙计们。

sentences.en: Because I'm creeped the f*** out.
sentences.zh: 因为我他妈的吓坏了。

sentences.en: Rishikesh Herway is the creator of Song Exploder, which I'm very proud to say is now a member of the Radiotopia Collective.
sentences.zh: 里希克什·赫尔威是《歌曲解密》的创作者，我很自豪地说，它现在是电台乌托邦集体的一员。

sentences.en: I'm so excited.
sentences.zh: 我太兴奋了。

sentences.en: Song Exploder is one of my favorite podcasts and the premise is just perfect.
sentences.zh: 《歌曲解密》是我最喜欢的播客之一，其构思简直完美。

sentences.en: Musicians take apart their songs piece by piece to tell the story of how they were made.
sentences.zh: 音乐家们一小段一小段地拆解他们的歌曲，来讲述它们是如何创作的故事。

sentences.en: If you've never heard Song Exploder before, I want to present what I think is my favorite episode so far, featuring John Roderick of the Long Winters.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前没听过《歌曲解密》，我想向你推荐我认为目前我最喜欢的一集，由“漫长冬天”乐队的约翰·罗德里克出演。

sentences.en: But I have a hard time picking a favorite.
sentences.zh: 但我很难挑出最喜欢的一集。

sentences.en: I really think that you should just download them all and pick your own favorite.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为你应该把它们全部下载下来，然后选出你自己的最爱。

sentences.en: Now, from Radiotopia, this is Song Exploder.
sentences.zh: 来自电台乌托邦，这里是《歌曲解密》。

sentences.en: My fellow Americans, this day has brought terrible news and great sadness to our country.
sentences.zh: 我同胞们的美国人，这一天给我们国家带来了可怕的消息和巨大的悲痛。

sentences.en: At 9 o'clock this morning, Mission Control in Houston lost contact with our space shuttle Columbia.
sentences.zh: 今天上午九点，休斯顿飞行控制中心与我们的哥伦比亚号航天飞机失去了联系。

sentences.en: A short time later, debris was seen falling from the skies above Texas.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，人们看到碎片从德克萨斯州上空坠落。

sentences.en: The Columbia is loSt.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚号失事了。

sentences.en: There are no survivors.
sentences.zh: 没有幸存者。

sentences.en: That was President George W.
sentences.zh: 那是时任总统乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush addressing the nation on February 1st, 2003.
sentences.zh: 布什在2003年2月1日向全国发表的讲话。

sentences.en: A couple years later, John Roderick, singer and songwriter of the Long Winters,
sentences.zh: 几年后，“漫长冬天”乐队的歌手兼词曲作者约翰·罗德里克，

sentences.en: recorded a song about the space shuttle Columbia on that day as it broke apart while reentering the Earth's atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 录制了一首歌，讲述了那天哥伦比亚号航天飞机在重新进入地球大气层时解体的事情。

sentences.en: It's called The Commander Thinks Aloud.
sentences.zh: 这首歌叫做《指挥官在沉思》。

sentences.en: This episode is made from an interview I did with John Roderick in front of a live audience in Seattle about how and why he made this song.
sentences.zh: 这一集取材于我在西雅图当着现场观众的面采访约翰·罗德里克的访谈，关于他是如何以及为何创作这首歌的。

sentences.en: I am John Roderick.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·罗德里克。

sentences.en: I had my pilot's license when I was 17.
sentences.zh: 我在17岁时就拿到了飞行员执照。

sentences.en: My dad was a small plane pilot.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一名小型飞机飞行员。

sentences.en: And that was the way my dad, that was one of the ways that we bonded, was in a small plane, you know, trying to make it over a mountain range.
sentences.zh: 那是父亲和我培养感情的方式之一，坐在一架小飞机里，你知道的，试图飞越山脉。

sentences.en: So I had a lot of experience in planes.
sentences.zh: 所以我有很多坐飞机的经验。

sentences.en: I always loved to fly, and when the nose comes off the ground, I always feel a charge.
sentences.zh: 我一直热爱飞行，当机轮离开地面时，我总是感到一阵兴奋。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be a person that was anxious about flying.
sentences.zh: 我不想成为一个对飞行感到焦虑的人。

sentences.en: Well, at that point in 2005, I guess, we were still pretty close to 9-11, and the space shuttle disaster followed pretty close on the heels of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在2005年那个时候，我想，我们离“9·11”事件过去没多久，而航天飞机灾难紧随其后发生。

sentences.en: But also, there were all those smaller disaster crashes.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有所有那些较小的灾难坠机事件。

sentences.en: The Alaska Airlines crash that happened off the coast of California where they lost their vertical stabilizer, the jack screw one.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加航空公司的坠机事故发生在加利福尼亚海岸附近，当时他们失去了垂直安定面，就是那个千斤螺丝的故障。

sentences.en: The pilots were aware there was a problem.
sentences.zh: 飞行员们意识到出了问题。

sentences.en: Everyone was aware there was a problem.
sentences.zh: 所有人都意识到出了问题。

sentences.en: It just flew around and then flipped upside down and plummeted into the ocean.
sentences.zh: 它只是在空中盘旋，然后翻转过来，坠入海洋。

sentences.en: And then there was the one off of Long Island where maybe the gas tank exploded.
sentences.zh: 接着是长岛附近的那起事故，可能是油箱爆炸了。

sentences.en: And then there was that Learjet that lost compression and everybody in it gone until it ran out of gas.
sentences.zh: 然后是那架失压的里尔喷气机，机上所有人都在飞机耗尽燃油前失去了意识。

sentences.en: And all of these disasters stuck with me, particularly the ones where there was a sense that the people on board knew that they were lost, but they were still alive.
sentences.zh: 所有这些灾难都深深烙印在我心中，尤其是那些能让人感觉到机上人员知道自己大难临头却还活着的时刻。

sentences.en: The unfolding, dawning realization like, you know, we're not getting out of this.
sentences.zh: 那种逐渐展开、豁然开朗的意识到，你知道的，我们逃不掉了。

sentences.en: And what's your reaction in that situation?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Do you scream?
sentences.zh: 你会尖叫吗？

sentences.en: You probably don't.
sentences.zh: 你大概不会。

sentences.en: Probably everybody is really calm in that situation.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，可能每个人都很冷静。

sentences.en: And so I pictured the astronauts on reentry.
sentences.zh: 所以我脑海中浮现出宇航员们重返大气层时的场景。

sentences.en: They knew there was something wrong with their ship.
sentences.zh: 他们知道飞船出了问题。

sentences.en: They were worried about it, but everybody had convinced them it was going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 他们为此感到担忧，但所有人都让他们相信一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And they're performing their duties.
sentences.zh: 他们正在履行职责。

sentences.en: They are having the peak experience of their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们正在经历一生中的巅峰体验。

sentences.en: And maybe one of the peak human experiences.
sentences.zh: 也许也是人类巅峰体验之一。

sentences.en: Like, we are coming back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们要回地球了。

sentences.en: Having just, like, looked down at Earth and had that feeling of how beautiful that kind of dumb little stuff is.
sentences.zh: 刚刚，像是低头看着地球，体会到那种看似愚蠢的小事是多么美好。

sentences.en: The beauty of the mundane, right?
sentences.zh: 平凡之美，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, boys and girls in cars and dogs and birds on lawns.
sentences.zh: 比如，开车的男孩女孩，草坪上的狗和鸟。

sentences.en: Like, seeing it maybe like no one else would ever see it.
sentences.zh: 就像，以一种也许其他人永远无法企及的方式去看待它。

sentences.en: Boys and girls in cars, dogs and birds on lawns.
sentences.zh: 开车的男孩女孩，草坪上的狗和鸟。

sentences.en: From here I can touch the sun.
sentences.zh: 从这里我能触摸到太阳。

sentences.en: Did you sit down with the idea that you were going to write a song about the space shuttle disaster?
sentences.zh: 你当时坐下来，是带着要写一首关于航天飞机灾难的歌的想法吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I didn't know how it was going to work.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道它会怎么发展。

sentences.en: Every once in a while you get one as a songwriter where you sit down at your instrument.
sentences.zh: 作为一个词曲作者，你偶尔会遇到这种情况：你坐在乐器前。

sentences.en: You have an idea.
sentences.zh: 你有一个想法。

sentences.en: You have a first line.
sentences.zh: 你有一句开头。

sentences.en: You sing it and compose the entire song in an hour.
sentences.zh: 你唱出来，然后在短短一小时内谱好了整首歌。

sentences.en: And then you go, I don't know where that came from.
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，我都不知道这灵感是从哪来的。

sentences.en: I resisted piano lessons as a kid, but sometime in high school I started to sit at the piano voluntarily when no one was home and try and figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我小时候很抗拒钢琴课，但上高中后某个时候，我开始在家里没人的时候主动坐在钢琴前，试图摸索着弹。

sentences.en: And I got as far as you could go if you were just practicing for 11 minutes at a time.
sentences.zh: 如果每次只练11分钟的话，我的水平也就只能到那一步了。

sentences.en: And I didn't really learn the piano until I was in my 30s.
sentences.zh: 直到我三十多岁的时候，我才真正学会了钢琴。

sentences.en: Learned the piano as much as I know it now.
sentences.zh: 学会了到现在为止我所掌握的钢琴水平。

sentences.en: In the early 90s, in Seattle especially, there was a mentality that you didn't want to over-learn your instrument.
sentences.zh: 在90年代初，尤其是西雅图，有一种心态，就是你不想把你的乐器学得太精通。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Because that was going to affect the authenticity of your feelings.
sentences.zh: 因为这会影响你情感的真实性。

sentences.en: And I embraced that hook, line, and sinker.
sentences.zh: 而我全盘接受了这种观念。

sentences.en: So the producer of this track was Tucker Martine.
sentences.zh: 所以这首歌的制作人是塔克·马丁（Tucker Martine）。

sentences.en: Tucker had just a stand-up parlor piano in his living room.
sentences.zh: 塔克的起居室里刚好有一台立式客厅钢琴。

sentences.en: And that was recorded in his living room.
sentences.zh: 而这首歌正是在他的起居室里录制的。

sentences.en: And now we would probably just record it, one measure, and loop it.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可能只会录制一个美声小节，然后做循环播放。

sentences.en: But at the time, I had to sit and play it for five minutes.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，我必须坐下来连续弹奏五分钟。

sentences.en: And then I would get to the end, and he'd be like, hmm, let's hit it again.
sentences.zh: 等我弹到最后，他会说，嗯，我们再来一次。

sentences.en: Eric Corson, Long Winter's bass player, and my chief musical partner.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·科森（Eric Corson），“长冬”（Long Winters）乐队的贝斯手，也是我的主要音乐合作伙伴。

sentences.en: He sat down at the microchord, which is not an instrument he knew.
sentences.zh: 他坐在微型合成器（microkorg）前，这不是他熟悉的乐器。

sentences.en: But he worked with it for a little bit and figured it out.
sentences.zh: 但他琢磨了一会儿，就上手了。

sentences.en: There are five or six moments in the song that without Eric's part, it would be so much less of a complete work.
sentences.zh: 这首歌里有五六个地方，如果没有埃里克的演奏，它作为一部完整作品的魅力就会大打折扣。

sentences.en: His part is very cinematic.
sentences.zh: 他的演奏非常有画面感。

sentences.en: As the song unfolds, it just starts to go sideways.
sentences.zh: 随着歌曲的展开，它开始走向失控。

sentences.en: And every successive verse, stuff is starting to break.
sentences.zh: 每一个接下来的段落，东西都开始损坏。

sentences.en: Most of the Long Winter's songs are about relationships, and they are intentionally difficult to parse.
sentences.zh: “长冬”乐队的大多数歌曲都是关于人际关系的，而且它们故意设计得难以解读。

sentences.en: Because they're meant to communicate in an emotional language rather than in a literal language.
sentences.zh: 因为它们旨在用情感语言而不是字面语言来交流。

sentences.en: And so as I was writing this song, as I made my way through the emotional story I was trying to tell,
sentences.zh: 所以在写这首歌的时候，当我梳理着我试图讲述的情感故事时，

sentences.en: I did arrive at a place where I was like, I need to give a clue here somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我确实到了一个地步，觉得我得在这里某处给出一个线索。

sentences.en: The crew compartment's breaking up.
sentences.zh: 乘员舱正在解体。

sentences.en: I was embarrassed to say the crew compartment's breaking up because I felt like it was too literal.
sentences.zh: 我很不好意思说出“乘员舱正在解体”这句话，因为我觉得这太字面化了。

sentences.en: And so to say the crew compartment's breaking up, the first time I went through it, I was just like, ah, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以要说出“乘员舱正在解体”，第一次过这部分时，我只是觉得，啊，你知道的。

sentences.en: But it needed it.
sentences.zh: 但它是必须的。

sentences.en: And the thing was, you sing it once, the second time everybody gets it, the third time they've heard it now,
sentences.zh: 问题是，你唱了一遍，第二遍大家就都懂了，第三遍他们已经听过了，

sentences.en: the fourth time they're like, okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 第四遍他们的反应是，行吧，好吧。

sentences.en: Fifth, sixth time it starts to get annoying.
sentences.zh: 第五、第六遍开始变得有点烦人了。

sentences.en: And then a new kind of gravity enters in.
sentences.zh: 然后一种新的重力介入了。

sentences.en: Seventh time.
sentences.zh: 第七遍。

sentences.en: You start to feel the emotion.
sentences.zh: 你开始感受到那种情感。

sentences.en: And when I perform it live, if I'm not careful, I will start to cry during that part.
sentences.zh: 当我在现场表演时，如果我稍不注意，在那部分我就会哭出来。

sentences.en: Those are real violins.
sentences.zh: 那些都是真的小提琴。

sentences.en: We tried to get a little string quartet to come and we ran several passes at it.
sentences.zh: 我们试着请一个小弦乐四重奏来，我们试录了好几遍。

sentences.en: We took that and played it double speed.
sentences.zh: 我们拿过那段录音，用双倍速度播放。

sentences.en: And they did their own version of this kind of swarm of bees.
sentences.zh: 他们做出了他们自己版本的这种“蜂群”似的声音。

sentences.en: So we didn't have a drummer and it was like, who should we get?
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时没有鼓手，就在想，我们该找谁？

sentences.en: Should we call that one guy?
sentences.zh: 我们要不要给那家伙打电话？

sentences.en: He was like, or I could get the best drummer in the country.
sentences.zh: 他当时说，或者我可以请到全国最好的鼓手。

sentences.en: Any producer would make that choice if he had Matt Chamberlain's number.
sentences.zh: 任何制作人如果有马特·张伯伦（Matt Chamberlain）的电话，都会做出这个选择。

sentences.en: And Tucker did.
sentences.zh: 而塔克有。

sentences.en: And he managed to not just introduce swing into it, but make this piano part, which on its own is very square and on top of the beat.
sentences.zh: 他不仅设法把摇摆乐（swing）的律动融入其中，还让这个钢琴声部——它本身非常死板且精准踩在拍子上——

sentences.en: And he played to it and introduced swing to it.
sentences.zh: 随着鼓声演奏，并被注入了摇摆的律动。

sentences.en: Played a little bit behind and a little bit with this tremendous sort of breath and energy.
sentences.zh: 稍微落后一点点演奏，又带着这种巨大的呼吸感和能量。

sentences.en: And watching it all happen was a revelation to me as a musician.
sentences.zh: 看着这一切发生，对我作为一个音乐人来说是个启示。

sentences.en: I understood how much I had to learn.
sentences.zh: 我明白了自己还有多少东西要学。

sentences.en: So what Matt did, he came in, he set up his drums and he had one microphone that he pulled out of a bag and set up himself.
sentences.zh: 所以马特来了之后，他架好鼓，从包里拿出一个麦克风，自己亲手设置好。

sentences.en: And we all just were watching him.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都只是看着他。

sentences.en: You know, like you would watch a Black Panther that came into your kitchen.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像你在厨房里看着一只美洲豹一样。

sentences.en: And he was like, what's it going to do?
sentences.zh: 当时大家都在想，他要做什么？

sentences.en: And he put the microphone in front of his drums and he was like, okay, you know, record me.
sentences.zh: 他把麦克风放在鼓前面，然后说，好了，你知道的，录吧。

sentences.en: And so he plays for about a minute and then he's like, play that back for me.
sentences.zh: 于是他演奏了一分钟左右，接着说，把那段放给我听听。

sentences.en: And he listens to the track for a minute.
sentences.zh: 他听了一分钟的音轨。

sentences.en: And then he stands up, he walks around and he moves the microphone imperceptibly.
sentences.zh: 然后他站起来，走来走去，极其微小地移动了麦克风的位置。

sentences.en: Sits back down and says, roll it.
sentences.zh: 重新坐下并说，开始吧。

sentences.en: And he plays all the way through the track.
sentences.zh: 接着他从头到尾完整地演奏了一遍。

sentences.en: And I was listening to it and going like, you know, I'm the songwriter and kind of the main guy here.
sentences.zh: 当时我在听，心里在想，你知道的，我是词曲作者，也是这里的主要负责人。

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, that was pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我就觉得，嗯，那挺不错的。

sentences.en: I mean, I've got some comments.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我有一些意见要发表。

sentences.en: And we got to the end and he was like, okay, roll it again.
sentences.zh: 等我们到了曲子末尾，他说，好吧，再录一遍。

sentences.en: You know, and he didn't wait to hear any comments from the songwriter, which is like, all right.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他根本没等词曲作者提出任何意见，感觉就像是，好吧。

sentences.en: He played through it again.
sentences.zh: 他又完整弹奏了一遍。

sentences.en: And I was like, that was interesting, you know, kind of variation.
sentences.zh: 然后我在想，那挺有意思的，你知道的，算是一种微调吧。

sentences.en: And he was like, give it to me again.
sentences.zh: 接着他说，再来一遍。

sentences.en: He did that five times.
sentences.zh: 他连续这样做了五次。

sentences.en: And then he's like, all right, you know, I'm coming into the control room.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，好了，你知道的，我要进控制室了。

sentences.en: And he comes in and he sits down and he's like, okay, pan those five tracks.
sentences.zh: 他走进来坐下，然后说，好，把那五个音轨进行声像定位。

sentences.en: Hard left, middle left, center, middle right, hard right.
sentences.zh: 最左、中左、中间、中右、最右。

sentences.en: In the order that I recorded that.
sentences.zh: 按照我录音的顺序。

sentences.en: Five mono drum parts.
sentences.zh: 五个单声道鼓声部。

sentences.en: And he had the foresight that there are drum fills that start on one track.
sentences.zh: 而且他很有远见地设计了那些从一个音轨开始的鼓点加花。

sentences.en: And continue through all five tracks.
sentences.zh: 并一直延续到全部五个音轨中。

sentences.en: So, you know, you hear about guys and you're like, oh, that guy's amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当你听到关于某些乐手的事迹时，你会想，哦，那家伙太了不起了。

sentences.en: But this was something truly amazing.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是真正令人惊叹的事情。

sentences.en: As part of his drum kit, I forgot to mention, he has a piece of rusty sheet metal just attached to a clamp.
sentences.zh: 我忘了提，作为他鼓组的一部分，他有一块生锈的薄铁皮，用一个夹子固定着。

sentences.en: And he starts to go up to this sheet metal like, and all of that sheet metal noise that he was creating.
sentences.zh: 他开始走向这块铁皮，做出那种动作，还有他制造的所有那些铁皮噪音。

sentences.en: The whole end of the tune, where the spaceship is coming apart, he was making that sound on the rusty metal.
sentences.zh: 整首歌的结尾，当飞船正在解体时，他就是在那个生锈的金属上制造出那种声音的。

sentences.en: He had a vision of the song that I didn't even have.
sentences.zh: 他对这首歌有着我甚至都不曾有过的构想。

sentences.en: You know, the title of the song wasn't clear until right about this point in the recording.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这首歌的名字直到录音的这个节点才最终明确下来。

sentences.en: And so then, if the commander's, you know, thinking aloud, why is he telling us this story?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果指挥官在，你知道的，自言自语，他为什么要给我们讲这个故事？

sentences.en: This is all I wanted to bring home.
sentences.zh: 这就是我只想带回家的全部。

sentences.en: This is all I wanted to bring home to you.
sentences.zh: 这就是我只想为你带回家的全部。

sentences.en: That's his last word, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想这是他的最后一句话。

sentences.en: Did you have a sense of who he was addressing when he says that?
sentences.zh: 当他说出这句话时，你对他的倾诉对象有概念吗？

sentences.en: I don't publicly out myself as a utopian and a people lover.
sentences.zh: 我不会公开表明自己是个乌托邦主义者或博爱主义者。

sentences.en: Because it's not my brand.
sentences.zh: 因为这不符合我的人设。

sentences.en: But I'm an idealist, and I love humanity, and I imagine us as all on a ship together,
sentences.zh: 但我是一个理想主义者，我热爱人类，我把我们想象成都在同一艘船上，

sentences.en: and all with a common cause.
sentences.zh: 所有人都有着共同的目标。

sentences.en: And space exploration seems like the ultimate expression of human beings doing their best work.
sentences.zh: 而太空探索似乎是人类竭尽所能的最极致体现。

sentences.en: So I imagine he's bringing that back to us, all of us.
sentences.zh: 所以我想象他把这一切带回给我们，带回给我们所有人。

sentences.en: It's something that, if we could only share that, the simple feeling of just like,
sentences.zh: 这是某种东西，如果我们只能分享那份单纯的感受，就像是，

sentences.en: why the hell do we go up into space?
sentences.zh: 我们到底为什么要飞向太空？

sentences.en: We go up into space to bring back that little tantalizing, like,
sentences.zh: 我们飞向太空是为了带回那种诱人的、像是……

sentences.en: vision of the Earth being a borderless place full of birds and boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 关于地球是一个充满鸟儿、男孩和女孩的无国界之地的愿景。

sentences.en: And now, here's The Commander Thinks Aloud by The Long Winters in its entirety.
